text:
mira-support: Customer reports repeated mid-stream disconnects on iOS when switching carriers / toggling Wi‑Fi. They get partial chunks then connection closes. App logs show: 
```
> request_id=req_9f2a client_ip=10.24.1.5 event=stream_abort reason=EOF tokens_emitted=246
```
Billing team flagged that partial tokens were charged. Customer on prod, high impact. Can someone triage? :eyes:

sam-phone: I can repro on my Pixel + Tethering. Steps: 1) start SSE generation ~60s, 2) flip phone from carrier->wifi, 3) after NAT rebinding we get no more chunks and client sees close. Repro is flaky but frequent on cellular handoffs.

mira-support: Pasted their request header for the failing call (sanitized):
```
GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <short-lived>
X-Req-Id: req_9f2a
Accept: text/event-stream
```
They said token refresh happens in app every 55s.

axel-sre: From infra logs around req_9f2a we see proxy 499s and a backend timeout right after a TCP FIN. Snip: 
```
2026-03-15T14:03:12Z proxy01 req=req_9f2a status=499 upstream=:0 client_ip=10.24.1.5
2026-03-15T14:03:12Z lb layer: detected client reset after NAT rebind
```
Seems like client side connection drops due to NAT/port rebind rather than server abort. 499 indicates client closed the conn.

leo-runtime: Two possible failure modes here: (1) NAT/ISP rotates IP -> TCP reset -> stream ends; (2) client refreshes auth mid-stream and reconnects with new token which makes it drop the prior SSE connection. Do we have evidence client rotates tokens during active streams?

sam-phone: Yes — customer SDK does a hard refresh by tearing down existing websocket/SSE and creating a new session to inject new Authorization header. They do that blindly at 55s. If a long generation runs past that window the client will close and start a fresh connection, causing mid-stream cutoff.

axel-sre: That matches. Two mitigation tracks: quick support workaround + eng fix. Quick workaround options:
- Ask client to postpone token refresh while there's an active stream (client-side change).
- Increase token TTL for that customer temporarily.
- Add server-side short resume window: accept reconnect within X seconds and resume last event if idempotency/session id provided.

leo-runtime: I'll open an internal engineering issue to evaluate server-side resume for SSEs and also investigate keeping a short grace period for auth rollover to avoid killing streams. Long term we likely want resume via session-id + last-event-id header. For immediate: we can allow a 10s linger on backend to accept reconnection from the same client IP+user after auth rotation.

mira-support: Customer asked about billing for the partial output they already received. Can billing confirm if partial tokens are refundable on aborted streams?

axel-sre: From infra POV, we can mark this as "client-abort" events and attach logs; I'm not billing owner but can attach traces to the case. Recommend support flag the customer's account and request a manual refund if needed while we patch.

leo-runtime: INF-2026-334 created and assigned to eng-runtime (priority: P1). Plan: 1) short-term: allow 10s reconnection grace to attempt resume (can be toggled per-customer); 2) mid-term: implement session resume via last-event-id/idempotency keys; 3) long-term: change SDK pattern to refresh tokens without dropping active streams. I'll post ETA in the issue.

mira-support: Thanks — I'll relay quick workaround (increase TTL or block refresh during active stream) to the customer and request logs + carrier+app version. Marking thread for escalation. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Escalation posted to #eng-runtime: INF-2026-334 — auto-notify leo-runtime, axel-sre.
